verdict.rationale: Bevy is a code-first Rust library, so its public crate API is the documented interface: first-party reference docs cover its types, traits and methods, and a probe confirms docs.rs gives static, crawlable API docs that an agent can drive through cargo without an editor. The API is pre-1.0 with breaking changes every release, and the first-party Bevy Remote Protocol for driving a running app is mentioned only in passing. missing for 10: a stable 1.0 API surface, first-party documentation of the Bevy Remote Protocol for runtime control, and independent hands-on corroboration of agent-driven use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Learn how to use Bevy's types, traits and methods using the in-depth reference documentation, complete with inline examples.
docs.rs/bevy gives fully static, crawlable API docs, and the code-first cargo workflow needs no editor for an agent to drive.
Bevy is just a normal Rust dependency.
